units.text: To show in which sections differences occur for files that are not source code for C or similar languages, use the ⟦0⟧ (⟦1⟧) option. ⟦2⟧ considers lines that match the ⟦3⟧-style regular expression ⟦4⟧ to be the beginning of a section of the file. units.text: This option does not automatically select an output format; in order to use it, you must select the context format (see ⟦0⟧Context Format⟦1⟧) or unified format (see ⟦2⟧Unified Format⟦3⟧). In other output formats it has no effect.
units.sourceHTML: This option does not automatically select an output format; in order to use it, you must select the context format (see Context Format) or unified format (see Unified Format). In other output formats it has no effect.

units.text: The ⟦0⟧ (⟦1⟧) option finds the nearest unchanged line that precedes each hunk of differences and matches the given regular expression. Then it adds that line to the end of the line of asterisks in the context format, or to the ‘⟦2⟧’ line in unified format. If no matching line exists, this option leaves the output for that hunk unchanged. If that line is more than 40 characters long, it outputs only the first 40 characters. You can specify more than one regular expression for such lines; ⟦3⟧ tries to match each line against each regular expression, starting with the last one given. This means that you can use ⟦4⟧ and ⟦5⟧ together, if you wish.
units.sourceHTML: The --show-function-line (-F) option finds the nearest unchanged line that precedes each hunk of differences and matches the given regular expression. Then it adds that line to the end of the line of asterisks in the context format, or to the ‘@@’ line in unified format. If no matching line exists, this option leaves the output for that hunk unchanged. If that line is more than 40 characters long, it outputs only the first 40 characters. You can specify more than one regular expression for such lines; diff tries to match each line against each regular expression, starting with the last one given. This means that you can use -p and -F together, if you wish.
